findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher rejects exactly the token IDs it should accept
findings.body: The new matcher in `isAccessTokenId` has two defects. First, the condition is inverted: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns false (no match) when the grant shortcut IS the expected one, and falls through to match for any other grant. Every call site (expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectAuthReqIdToToken) passes the shortcut that will actually be present, so all of these event assertions will fail on valid tokens. Second, the offset is wrong: the 6-char context is sessionType(0-1) + tokenType(2-3) + grantType(4-5), so the grant shortcut is at substring(4, 6), not substring(3, 5). With the inverted logic fixed, the code as written would compare chars 3-4 (second char of token type + first char of grant shortcut) and never match any valid grant shortcut. It should be `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.

findings.title: Duplicate null-check on grantType leaves rawTokenId unvalidated
findings.body: The constructor contains `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null grantType not allowed");` twice in a row (lines 72-73), and the second one has the message "Null rawTokenId not allowed" but still checks grantType. As a result, rawTokenId is never null-checked despite the intent, and a null rawTokenId would produce a token ID ending in "null" or cause a later NPE in encodeTokenId. The second check should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`.

findings.title: Copy constructor Context(Context) removed without replacement
findings.body: The diff removes the public copy constructor `public Context(Context context)` from OAuth2GrantType.Context and adds the grantType field only to the primary constructor. Any existing code (in Keycloak itself or in custom OAuth2GrantType provider implementations deployed by users) that wraps or re-creates a Context via `new Context(existingContext)` will no longer compile, and the new grantType field would also be lost by such a copy even if re-added manually. This is an SPI interface in server-spi-private, but the removal is a silent breaking change that should either be restored (copying grantType as well) or called out.

findings.title: Token ID encoding applied to every AccessToken including paths where GRANT_TYPE context is never set
findings.body: initToken now unconditionally encodes the token ID via the encoder, reading Constants.GRANT_TYPE from the ClientSessionContext. That attribute is only set in the OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse path, ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType, PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType, StandardTokenExchangeProvider, and refresh validation. Tokens created through other paths that call createClientAccessToken — e.g. the implicit/hybrid flow in AuthorizationEndpoint, or any custom protocol/token service calling TokenManager directly — will silently get grant type "na" baked into the token ID. That may be acceptable, but more critically, any AccessToken whose context yields an unknown grant type that is not in the encoder's shortcut map causes encodeTokenId to throw IllegalStateException, failing token issuance with a 500. If a deployment adds a grant-type-like flow that sets Constants.GRANT_TYPE to a value not registered as an OAuth2GrantType (or sets it before the factory's maps are populated/refreshed in a cluster where provider registration differs), token creation breaks entirely. The encoder should fall back to the "na" shortcut instead of throwing when encoding.
